sense: put in order, plan out (things, one’s time)

evidence: Plin. Ep. 9.36.1: quemadmodum in Tuscīs diem aestāte dispōnam
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to place here and there, to set in different places, to distribute regularly, to dispose, arrange”. An orderly life is vīta disposita (Plin. Ep. 3.1.2).
Lewis & Short: “to order, set in order, arrange, adjust, dispose, regulate”. The household word for tidying (see tidy up).

terms.gloss: sort out, set in order (papers, the calendar)
evidence: Ov. F. 1.27: tempora dīgereret cum conditor urbis

phrases.latin: quaeris, quemadmodum in Tuscīs diem aestāte dispōnam
phrases.english: You ask how I organise my day in summer at my Tuscan villa.

phrases.latin: mē autem ut certus sīderum cursus ita vīta hominum disposita dēlectat
phrases.english: As the sure course of the stars delights me, so does an orderly life.

phrases.latin: nihil esse pulchrius in omnī ratiōne vītae dispositiōne atque ōrdine
phrases.english: Nothing in any walk of life is finer than arrangement and order.

sources: Lewis & Short: dispono · Lewis & Short: ordino · Lewis & Short: digero
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-plinius, loci-cato (for Columella), loci-ovidius), checked against the editions named there.
